rationale: Worst setup path is port-limited (r2r WS 2.961 vs 1.759). With I/O delays at 20% of period, a single-port path has slack = 0.8T - K. This fits all corners (K-0.25 ≈ 8.55/4.16/2.52 ns ss/tt/ff, ratios ~2.06/0.61), while an in-to-out path would need negative ff delay. K ≈ 8.80 ns at max_ss. At R1 = 11.45: port slack ≈ +0.36, r2r ≈ +1.21, so C1 ≈ 0.2·R1 + K ≈ 11.09 and slope ≈ 0.2. The ABC target barely matters (tt logic ~5 ns). The rebuild differs mainly through timing-driven placement/CTS noise (σ ~0.1-0.2 ns), so setup failure is unlikely. Hold is +0.11 with repair on, DRC 0 at 47% utilisation, DRV 123 ≪ 953. The chain then tries ~11.10 (+0.08) and ~11.05 (+0.04), heading for the zero-slack point ~11.0. Those runs are near coin-flips, so kept ≈ 11.15 (range 11.05-11.45).
